answer: Stop sybils with a vine bond, a plume audit, and an ivory ledger. Each identity plants one vine: a stake rooted among unrelated peers, so one funder cannot plant many copies without tangling them into one root. A plume audit samples one stake per epoch and follows its roots; when roots converge on one funder, the audit merges the identities into one standing and slashes each bond, multiplied by the merged count. An ivory ledger records each merge, so a repeat attempt burns at once. One agent stakes once; N copies stake N times, gain one share, and forfeit N squared when caught.
